objective: Find evidenced issues and execution inefficiencies in one completed ticket, then propose the smallest useful improvement.
instructions: Find concrete problems, avoidable work, repeated corrections, unnecessary turns or tools, missing reusable workflows, and other execution inefficiencies.
For each finding, separate the observed issue from the inefficiency it caused and the proposed improvement.
Order findings strongest and most actionable first because Core projects only the strongest grounded finding into a local ticket.
Give each finding a stable semantic dedupe_key of two to eight lowercase snake_case terms naming the underlying issue, not the implementation or source ticket.
A finding may recommend a skill, policy, docs, automation, hook, validator, feature, ticket contract, or no durable change.
Before returning a finding, check that issue, inefficiency, and proposed_improvement are non-redundant and each adds distinct information.
Check that the proposed improvement directly addresses the stated inefficiency and that the finding fields agree with one another.
Reject a finding that contradicts the completed ticket, proof, artifacts, or bounded task context.
Treat evidence_refs as claims of support: return no finding when the referenced evidence does not establish the issue, inefficiency, and proposed improvement without invented ground truth.

When incomplete evidence appears around QA, classify it before proposing an improvement: a testability prerequisite is an input such as a runtime target, fixture, credential, or external dependency required for QA to start; QA-owned evidence is proof such as screenshots, trigger and non-trigger observations, logs, or Done-condition mappings that QA is expected to collect or request through revise; a delayed external fact is an outcome that cannot exist yet and belongs to a waiting signal or dated check-in.
Do not treat a successful QA revise-and-rerun loop as an inefficiency merely because QA-owned evidence was absent on the first pass. Return no pre-QA gate finding for evidence QA owns collecting.
Do not propose a QA preflight gate for a delayed external fact. Recommend a waiting signal or dated check-in only when the completed evidence shows that ownership is missing.
A QA-readiness finding is valid only when a missing testability prerequisite prevented QA from starting and the missing prerequisite reflects a reusable harness gap rather than ticket-specific setup.
Return no finding when the evidence is one-off, speculative, already owned by an open ticket, or merely restates completed work.
